name: worker-in-action-test-5a590dbd54/worker-in-action-v.bal
spec_references: Supported language features (subset 10) / Module-level declarations: Supports `client`, `service`, `isolated`, `readonly` and `distinct` [`class-type-quals`]
Supported language features (subset 10) / Module-level declarations: Supports [`remote-method-defn`] for client classes and `resource-method-defn` for service classes
Supported language features (subset 10) / Expressions: [Client remote method call action]
Supported language features (subset 10) / Statements: lists supported statements without named worker declarations or worker send statements
Supported language features (subset 10) / Expressions: lists Start action and Wait action, but no worker receive action
reason: Named workers and their asynchronous sends/receives are essential to all three asserted outputs and are not covered by the subset's positive lists. Client classes, remote methods/calls and runtime:sleep are explicitly covered, but do not establish worker support. The REACHED assertion additionally depends on propagating an early default-worker error to a pending worker receive and allowing that worker to update module state.
unsupported_constructs: Named worker declarations, including worker return types
Worker send statements and receive actions involving named workers and the default worker (`function`)
Default-worker early-return error propagation to a worker receive and concurrent completion behavior
test_design_notes: Mixed scope: supported remote action/class and runtime:sleep constructs are combined with unsupported worker messaging in one case.
The REACHED output relies on a fixed 0.2-second sleep for worker progress; it has no explicit completion synchronization.
No obvious output-marker mismatch; io:println is instrumentation.
